note: Best-effort mappings of common MITRE ATT&CK techniques to control failures and compliance obligations across NIST 800-53, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, SEC, and ISO 27001. Not legal advice — confirm with your auditor.

T1566.001.obligation: Train workforce to recognize spearphishing; report and respond to suspected phishing attempts.
Monitor inbound email for malicious attachments/links and alert on detections.
Ensure all malicious software is identified and prevented via anti-phishing controls.
Implement a security awareness and training program including phishing.
Implement appropriate technical measures to ensure ongoing confidentiality of personal data processed via email.
Safeguard customer records against phishing-borne unauthorized access.
Ensure users are made aware of security threats via awareness training including phishing.

T1059.001.obligation: Block/contain malicious code, including suspicious PowerShell execution; alert on bypass.
Audit PowerShell script-block logging (EID 4104) and command invocation (EID 4103).
Restrict access to systems running PowerShell to least privilege.
Implement audit controls recording PowerShell-based access to ePHI systems.
Detect and limit automated processing of personal data via unapproved scripts.
Detect script-based exfiltration of nonpublic customer information.
Monitor and detect misuse of legitimate administrative tools (Living-off-the-Land).

T1003.001.obligation: Enforce access enforcement to prevent unauthorized LSASS memory credential dumping.
Detect LSASS access by non-system processes and alert.
Secure all authentication factors; prevent credential extraction from memory.
Verify person/entity seeking access to ePHI is not extracting credentials.
Protect credentials used to access personal data against memory-dump extraction.
Prevent unauthorized credential extraction that could compromise customer data.
Secure user authentication credentials against theft including memory-resident dumping.

T1486.obligation: Conduct backups of information to enable recovery from ransomware encryption.
Execute incident handling for ransomware; isolate affected systems immediately.
Implement and test an incident response plan covering ransomware events.
Establish and implement a data backup and recovery plan for ransomware.
Notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours if ransomware breaches personal data.
Notify affected customers of a ransomware breach of customer data within regulatory timelines.
Implement verified backups and a tested ransomware recovery procedure.

T1021.002.obligation: Control and monitor remote access via SMB/Admin shares to authorized users only.
Transmit confidentiality via approved channels; SMB should be restricted at perimeter.
Restrict inbound/outbound SMB traffic at network boundaries.
Implement encryption for ePHI transmitted over SMB across untrusted networks.
Protect personal data in transit; restrict administrative share access.
Safeguard customer information accessed via administrative shares.
Protect information in transit and restrict remote administrative share use.

T1071.001.obligation: Monitor and filter outbound web/HTTP C2 traffic at boundary protection devices.
Detect anomalous HTTP beaconing to unknown destinations.
Restrict outbound traffic from the cardholder data environment.
Protect against malicious HTTP-based communication from ePHI systems.
Detect unauthorized exfiltration of personal data over HTTP channels.
Detect exfiltration of customer nonpublic personal information via web protocols.
Monitor and restrict outbound network traffic to enforce permitted destinations only.

T1562.001.obligation: Restrict disabling or tampering with security tools; alert on AV/EDR stoppage.
Detect impairment of security sensors and alert on tampering.
Ensure anti-malware mechanisms remain active and cannot be disabled by end users.
Protect against malicious software including tampering with protection mechanisms.
Maintain the integrity and availability of personal-data protection controls.
Detect disabling of safeguards protecting customer information.
Protect against malware including detection of security-control impairment.

T1070.001.obligation: Review audit logs for tampering/incomplete records and alert on deletion.
Protect audit information and logging components from unauthorized modification.
Implement automated audit trails including all modifications to audit logs.
Audit log clearing/tampering affecting ePHI access records.
Maintain processing records; detect deletion of logs that document processing.
Preserve electronic records; log tampering may violate books-and-records obligations.
Protect logging and monitoring information from unauthorized modification.

T1048.002.obligation: Monitor and control information flows over DNS to detect exfiltration.
Detect anomalous DNS traffic consistent with tunneled exfiltration.
Restrict outbound DNS from the cardholder data environment to known resolvers.
Implement controls to detect ePHI exfiltration over DNS tunnels.
Notify supervisory authority within 72 hours if DNS exfiltration breaches personal data.
Detect exfiltration of customer information via DNS tunneling.
Monitor and restrict DNS traffic to detect data exfiltration.

T1053.005.obligation: Restrict use of Scheduled Task for persistence and alert on suspicious creations.
Audit Scheduled Task creation, modification, and execution events (EID 4698/4702).
Restrict privileges to create Scheduled Tasks to authorized administrators.
Audit Scheduled Task use to detect unauthorized persistence on ePHI systems.
Detect unauthorized persistence enabling access to personal-data systems.
Detect persistence on systems holding customer nonpublic personal information.
Monitor for misuse of legitimate OS features (Scheduled Tasks) for persistence.
